messages:
incident-bot: PAGER P1 -- hosted-prod pool 'hosted-1' reporting repeated KV cache OOMs and elevated 5xx on /v1/generate (5xx spike > 12% over 3m). See metrics: https://dash.internal/redwood/kvcache/hosted-1
Maya (oncall): I have the pager. Paging @Julia, @Sam, @Priya, @CS-Leah. Kicking off triage.
Julia (eng-sre): Logs show a rapid jump in kvcache_allocated_bytes from ~180GB -> ~980GB in ~2 minutes. Eviction loop lagging. Prefetch queue depth extremely high.
Sam (eng-runtime): Any recent rollout? Checking feature flags and runtime diffs. I see continuous-prefetch toggled to true in hosted-1 8m ago (change cf-4451). Also a batching tweak merged this morning.
Priya (eng-ml): Correlating traces: several requests with concatenated user/system prompts (auto-append from client) hitting effective context sizes >120k tokens. These are streaming concat patterns.
CS-Leah: Customer-reported impact: Acme experiencing truncated streams and connector failures starting 00:27 UTC. Ticket #INC-ACME-137 opened.
Maya (oncall): Severity P1. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous prefetch on hosted-1, 2) enforce soft server-side prompt length cap for new requests, 3) throttle batching window and reduce per-batch token max, 4) accelerate eviction sweep. Julia/Sam assignable?
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll flip prefetch off for hosted-1 now. Using adminctl: 

adminctl feature-set --name continuous_prefetch --scope hosted-1 --value false --reason "incident: kvcache OOM"

deploy-bot: adminctl change queued: change-id ff-6891 applied to 12 nodes.
Julia (eng-sre): Bumping eviction frequency and eviction_target_ratio. Running infra script: 

rgctl update-kvcache --pool hosted-1 --evict-interval 12s --evict-ratio 0.25

infra-bot: rgctl job started job-9973. ETA ~25s.
Priya (eng-ml): As an emergency guard I'm reducing batching.max_window_tokens from 65536 -> 7168 for hosted-1. Patching runtime config now.
Sam (eng-runtime): Patch applied. Also enabling a temporary reject rule for single-request prompt_size > 200k tokens to prevent runaway single requests.
Maya (oncall): CS-Leah, please send a short note to Acme: we have temporary throttles in place to protect stability, expecting restoration in ~30m, will follow up with RCA.
CS-Leah: Sent: "We're throttling very long-context requests as an emergency mitigation. We'll follow up with an update and ETA on full resolution in 30 minutes"
Julia (eng-sre): Metrics update: OOM logs dropped dramatically on 4/5 nodes within 90s of prefetch disable. 5xx rate down from 16% -> 4% in the last 2m. kvcache_allocated_bytes decreasing towards baseline (~360GB).
Sam (eng-runtime): Tail latency increased a bit due to eviction thrash while caches compact; that's expected. Keeping prefetch off until we have better circuit-breakers.
Maya (oncall): Good. Next: collect offending request ids and traces for RCA. Priya, can you pull top traces and upload?
Priya (eng-ml): Uploading top-100 long-context traces and request payloads to S3: https://s3.internal/redwood/incidents/1993004444/long_traces/index.html and s3://internal/incidents/1993004444/payloads.tgz
Priya (eng-ml): Preliminary breakdown: ~45% of problematic traffic traced to 6 customers who stream-append conversation segments client-side with no size checks. We'll propose server-side max_prompt_tokens and prefix-detection.
Julia (eng-sre): I'll file a follow-up for prefetch backpressure and rollout safety: trigger prefetch-disable when any kvcache shard > 400GB OR prefetch_queue_length > 2000, and add alerting.

Issue: KVCACHE-1401
Title: Prefetch backpressure + rollout safety for hosted runtime
Labels: p1,kvcache,production

Sam (eng-runtime): Suggest rollback of the recent batching changes (roll back to continuous_batching.v1) for hosted-1 until we have server-side guards. Starting rollback now.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: job rb-2330.
deploy-bot: rollback complete across hosted-1 nodes.
Julia (eng-sre): After rollback and eviction tuning, 5xxs steady <1%, kvcache bytes stable ~310-380GB. Looks mitigated.
Maya (oncall): Impact summary: partial failures for a subset of hosted customers (including Acme), duration ~22 minutes from alert to stabilization. Mitigations: disabled prefetch, reduced batch window and max tokens, added temporary prompt-size reject, increased eviction frequency, rolled back batching rollout.
CS-Leah: Informed Acme that mitigations are complete and asked them to confirm no further errors. They acknowledged and will monitor.
Maya (oncall): Handoff and owners: RCA + model-pattern analysis: Priya; Prefetch backpressure + runtime changes: Sam; Eviction & infra hardening: Julia; Customer comms & status: CS-Leah.
Maya (oncall): I'll draft the incident note and a public postmortem draft. Keeping the pager open for 90 minutes for monitoring, then close. Thanks all for quick response :clap:
